correctness.rationale: Frozen RESULT.md line 21 is false where it says intermediate sizes may be skipped. The replacement RESULT.md proves the opposite. The projector calculation gives a positive diagonal, nonpositive other entries and zero row sum, so the symmetric kernel has both endpoint norms equal to twice the maximum diagonal. Maximizing the two weighted exponentials separately gives the sharp bound; different rates make it strict for every nonsingleton row, and finiteness and endpoint decay make it strict for the supremum if no singleton exists. The logarithmic time derivatives of the rescaled rows h_m are in [m−1,m) and zero for m=1, giving the unique directional crossings. For fixed t>0, write h_m=(n−m)e^(mt)(1−g_t(m)), where g_t(m)=∫₀ᵗe^(−mu)du lies in (0,1) and g_t″>0 for real 1≤m<n. This makes log h_m strictly concave in size; at the outer crossing for a<b<c the middle row beats both, so t_ab<t_ac<t_bc. Consequently all adjacent crossings are global, exactly two adjacent sizes tie at each, and every size is uniquely active on an open interval. The last active row recovers n from the larger exponential rate, or the sole rate for an all-singleton graph; distinct positive rates are uniquely extracted from the exact tail. At fixed n, analytic agreement on any single-size interval forces equal zero-time limits 2(n−m), identifying each size. The two graphs have equal n and size sets but unequal multiplicity of eigenvalue 18. The original numerical checker was inspected and not executed, and its pairwise tests cannot adjudicate the frozen skip assertion; the replacement proof establishes the conclusions without it.
